name: Saint Marcellus I
history: Pope after the persecution of Diocletian had left the Roman Church scattered and without a bishop for several years. Marcellus reorganised its parishes and insisted that Christians who had denied the faith under threat should do penance before being readmitted. The bitter quarrels that followed led the emperor Maxentius to banish him, and he died in exile. He is venerated as a martyr.
life: Marcellus was a Roman priest elected bishop of Rome around 308, after a vacancy caused by the persecution. He found the Church in disorder. He divided the city into districts, each with its church and priests, to prepare people for baptism and to care for the burial of the martyrs. The hardest question was what to do with the lapsed, the many who had offered sacrifice to the gods to save their lives. Marcellus held a middle course: they could return, but only after real penance. Some thought this too hard, others too soft, and the disturbances grew so violent that Maxentius sent him away. A later tradition says he was condemned to work as a groom in the stables of the imperial post. Pope Damasus wrote an epitaph praising him as a true shepherd who would not let the lapsed return without repentance. His relics rest in the church of San Marcello in Rome.
prayerTo: Saint Marcellus, shepherd of a wounded Church, you called the fallen home with both mercy and truth. Pray for all who have drifted from the faith, that they may find the way back through repentance. Pray for me, that I may never take God’s forgiveness lightly, and that I may help to rebuild what has been broken. Amen.
penance: Pray today for someone who has left the practice of the faith, and make a small sacrifice for them, such as going without a snack or a drink you enjoy.
meditation: Marcellus would neither pretend that sin did not matter nor shut the door on the sinner. Which of the two do you find harder?
prayer: O Lord, we beseech You, graciously hear the prayers of Your people, that we may be helped by the merits of blessed Marcellus, Your Pope and Martyr, whose sufferings we celebrate. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
